Q: Incremental data sync from Dynamics CRM entity without modifiedon or versionnumber A:

You’ve basically hit a limitation of Microsoft Dynamics 365. If there’s no modifiedon or versionnumber, there’s no clean way to track changes incrementally. That’s exactly what those fields are meant for. Your current approach (full load + compare) is honestly what most people end up doing in this case. It’s not perfect, but it works. If you want to improve it a bit, you can check if change tracking is available for that entity, or add a custom “last modified” field if it’s a custom entity. Otherwise, the only real option is what you’re already doing, just try to optimize it with better indexing or smaller batches.

Q: https://www.realestate.com.au/ not permitting web scraping? A:

This usually happens because realestate.com.au uses heavy JavaScript rendering along with anti-bot protection (like Cloudflare/Akamai), so when Selenium opens the page, it may load a blank or restricted version instead of actual content. It’s not just about scraping permission—the site actively blocks automated requests.

A few things you can try: use proper headers (especially user-agent), switch to non-headless mode to check for CAPTCHA, and use explicit waits instead of time.sleep():

from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC

WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.presence_of_element_located((By.TAG_NAME, "body"))
)

You can also try tools like undetected-chromedriver or use residential proxies if blocking continues. In some cases, rendering the page fully (or using Playwright) works better.

We faced a similar issue while working on real estate data extraction projects like experion windchants where the site initially returned incomplete or blocked content. By adjusting headers, using proper waits, and avoiding headless mode, we were able to extract the required data successfully.

Also, keep in mind that scraping such platforms may violate their Terms of Service, so checking for an official API is always a safer approach.

Q: Define Color of ObjectStatus Text A:

I would like to turn city's name color into red if it's "Berlin".

<ObjectStatus xmlns="sap.m"
   state="{= ${ToSupplier/Address/City} === 'Berlin' ? 'Error' : undefined}"
   text="{ToSupplier/Address/City}"
   inverted="true"
/>

The control sap.m.ObjectStatus supports various colors via the property state which awaits:

Semantic Value State Colors

  • "Error" (reddish)
  • "Warning" (orangish)
  • "Success" (greenish)
  • "Information" (blueish / highlighting, since v1.60.1)

Indication Colors

  • "Indication01" … "Indication05" (Since v1.62)
  • "Indication06" … "Indication08" (Since v1.75)
  • "Indication09" … "Indication20" (Since v1.120)

Here, the colors are still pre-defined by the theme but their semantic meanings depend on the application.

In contrast to the ValueState, the semantic meaning must be defined by the application.

➡️ Samples

In case other colors are required, take a look at https://stackoverflow.com/a/42232902/5846045. However, I'd strongly encourage to avoid custom CSS if the app is going to be used within an application container, such as SAP Fiori launchpad, where applications need consistent UI/UX patterns.

See also:

  • Fiori design guideline: How To Use Semantic Colors / Industry-Specific Colors
  • UI5 documentation: Theming

Q: Explain the effects of export LANG, LC_CTYPE, and LC_ALL A:

See at the Environment Variables ¹ of UNIX Specification page:

  • LANG This variable determines the locale category for native language, local customs and coded character set in the absence of the LC_ALL and other LC_* (LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) environment variables. This can be used by applications to determine the language to use for error messages and instructions, collating sequences, date formats, and so forth.

  • LC_ALL This variable determines the values for all locale categories. The value of the LC_ALL environment variable has precedence over any of the other environment variables starting with LC_ (LC_COLLATE, LC_CTYPE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME) and the LANG environment variable.

  • LC_CTYPE This variable determines the locale category for character handling functions, such as tolower(), toupper() and isalpha(). This environment variable determines the interpretation of sequences of bytes of text data as characters (for example, single- as opposed to multi-byte characters), the classification of characters (for example, alpha, digit, graph) and the behaviour of character classes. Additional semantics of this variable, if any, are implementation-dependent.

¹: The OP's first link is from 1997 version, while this one is from 2008 version.

Q: How do I get the module instance for a class in Python? A:

I would like to obtain the __path__ for the __module__ for self (which in this case will be the subclass). Problem is, __module__ returns a str rather than the module instance itself

For this task you need the sys module to get the module object by its name.
The following code demonstrates how you can achieve this:


import sys

class Test:
    ...

# Create an instance (equals self)
instance = Test()
# Get the class of this instance
class_of_instance = type(instance)
# Proof that it is the class of the instance
print(class_of_instance == instance.__class__)
# Get module name of class
name_of_module_class_was_defined_in = class_of_instance.__module__
# Proof it is the same module
print(__name__ == name_of_module_class_was_defined_in)
# Get the module-object
module_object = sys.modules[__name__]

Q: React Native Android error: java.lang.String cannot be cast to java.lang.Boolean (Expo app, no terminal stacktrace) A:

This error:

java.lang.String cannot be cast to java.lang.Boolean

means a string ("true"/"false") is being used where a boolean (true/false) is expected.

Since your Switch code looks correct, the issue is most likely coming from API data (Webflow).

🔥 Common cause

Your API might return:

"isEnabled": "true" // ❌ string

Instead of:

"isEnabled": true // ✅ boolean

Passing this to Switch crashes on Android.

✅ Fix

Convert values to boolean:

const safeBoolean = value === true || value === "true";

<Switch value={safeBoolean} />

🔍 Also check

Picker values (don’t mix string/boolean)

Props passed to child components

Log values:

console.log(typeof isEnabled, isEnabled);

🧠 Key point

👉 Android is strict → strings cannot be used as booleans

👉 This usually comes from API data, not your UI code

🚀 Tip

While debugging API responses, formatting JSON helps catch issues like "true" vs true quickly:

👉 https://toolhub.fyi/tool/json-formatter
